statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress rises to 38, moderate, on a verified overnight escalation in US-Canada trade alongside the carried rates, energy and US-Iran backdrop.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows at 14.89, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z Friday and reopens Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly sixteen hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the backdrop. The material change this hour is new and verified rather than a re-reading of Friday: US-Canada trade negotiations collapsed late Friday and 50% US tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods took effect at midnight ET under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, with Prime Minister Carney stating Canada will match them dollar for dollar. That development arrived after the cash close and cannot be priced by any equity venue before the Sunday reopen, so it is carried as Stress and as unpriced weekend information, not as Tail. The rest of the backdrop is unchanged and re-confirmed: the 2Y/10Y/30Y curve at 4.24%/4.74%/5.28%, WTI at 87.06 and Brent at 94.39 after a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%, and a week-ahead stack of Core PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday, Nvidia after the Wednesday close, and Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on Friday. Two further Monday checkpoints sit just past this horizon: a US Treasury press conference detailing measures against Iran, for which no exact time has been published, and a reported 60-day ceasefire expiry. None of it falls inside the hours published here.
headline: Seventh consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, while a verified overnight collapse in US-Canada trade talks and 50% tariffs effective at midnight ET lift Stress to 38 with Tail unchanged at the closed-venue floor.
body:
CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run to 2026-08-23T06:00:00Z. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. That settlement is corroborated by separately reported Friday index moves: the S&P 500 at 7,674.37, +0.43%, the Nasdaq Composite at 26,180.45, +0.43%, and the Dow at 53,277.01, +0.98% on healthcare strength.

The new information this hour is a trade-policy escalation that arrived after the cash close. US-Canada negotiations were suspended late Friday, and 50% US tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods took effect at midnight ET under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, a provision reported as never previously deployed. Prime Minister Carney said Canada will match the tariffs dollar for dollar and recalled negotiators to Ottawa, while the US Trade Representative said Canada introduced late demands that upended a draft deal. Because the order took effect while every equity venue in scope was shut, it is unpriced information: it raises Stress and the weight of the eventual Sunday repricing, and it cannot create an observable Nasdaq-100 price path inside this horizon.

The carried backdrop is rates-led rather than equity-led. The 30-year Treasury yield closed at 5.28%, near its highest since 2007, the 10-year at 4.74% testing 20-month highs, and the 2-year at 4.24%. Crude held its war-premium levels, with WTI at 87.06 and Brent at 94.39 after both benchmarks gained more than 5% for a second consecutive week on the Strait of Hormuz disruption. The US-Iran impasse is unresolved: the Treasury Secretary has said he will detail coordinated economic-isolation measures at a press conference on Monday, no exact time has been published, and Iranian officials have publicly dismissed the plan. Reporting also places a 60-day ceasefire expiry on Monday.

Cross-asset context collected at 07:20Z is complete and internally consistent but explicitly latest-session and delayed, so it is used only as confirmation: index futures marks of NQ +0.30%, ES +0.38% and YM +0.95% with VIX futures -1.68% reproduce Friday's close rather than any live path. Breadth was mixed rather than aligned, with software up over 1% while the semiconductor group averaged -0.70% and Nvidia fell 0.98%, which reduces directional conviction rather than amplifying Tail. No amplifier of the kind that would justify a higher Tail is present, because none can be observed while no venue prints a price.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 20 hourly assessments are available and 4 clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable, two in the 21 August late-morning window and two in the 22 August pre-dawn window. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the European morning, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, then a step down to 10, 5 and finally 4 as the venue moved into its 21:00Z Friday halt and stayed there. Stress traced the same arc in reverse scale, easing from the high fifties to the mid thirties as equity-structure risk was replaced by carried rates, energy and weekend headline risk. No danger window was published in any of those hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the horizon ends at 2026-08-23T06:00:00Z, roughly sixteen hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress opens at 38, one step above the previous hour because the overnight US-Canada tariff escalation is verified and entirely unpriced, eases to a 36 trough through the quietest Saturday hours, and then climbs to 45 by the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens. Its composition is the tariff exchange plus the 30-year at 5.28% near a 2007 high, the 10-year at 4.74% testing 20-month highs, crude near 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse with a Monday Treasury announcement outstanding. Confidence starts at 86 and decays to 79 by the final slot as the verified Friday dataset ages; the closed-venue conclusion itself stays effectively certain throughout. Dominant mode is normal in every slot. The first genuine test arrives beyond this horizon, at the Sunday reopen and then Monday's scheduled items, and will be scored on observed structure rather than assumed in advance.
